sentences.text: The species Palintropus retusus is known from a single proximal coracoid bone discovered in the Lance Formation of Wyoming.
This type species is based on that specific coracoid from the Lance Formation, which dates to 65.5 million years ago.
Related unnamed species from the Campanian of Alberta include coracoids and a proximal scapula found between 76.5 and 75 million years ago.
Scientists initially placed this genus in the wastebin genus Cimolopteryx before reclassifying it.
Pierce Brodkorb assigned the current name in 1970, following an earlier affiliation with Apatornis in 1963.
A 2009 cladistic analysis by Longrich and colleagues suggested Palintropus is a primitive bird related to Apsaravis and belongs in the family Palintropiformes.
The relationships of Palintropus remain poorly determined mainly due to the scarcity of available material.
The Paleobiology Database classifies Palintropus under the class Reptilia.
That same database lists the parent group of Palintropus as Quercymegapodiidae.
The time range for Palintropus is recorded as Campanian to Campanian, from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.
Some researchers believe Palintropus is an early member of the Charadriiformes, similar to birds of the Western Interior Seaway.
An alternate theory suggests Palintropus is a galliform, possibly a quercymegapodiid.
It is sometimes believed to be a primitive member of the Charadriiformes order, similar to birds of the subtropical coastlands of the Western Interior Seaway.
An alternative theory is that it is a Galliforme, perhaps a quercymegapodiid.
The family assigned to Palintropus in the Paleobiology Database is Quercymegapodiidae.
